authority.quote: Publishing workflows that use `kunobi-ninja/kache-action` are not classified as cache-aware.

proof.red_test:
import json, subprocess, pathlib, sys
root=pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
binary=next(root.glob('uv-cache/archive-v0/*/bin/zizmor'))
file=sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv)>1 else 'kache-publish.yml'
p=subprocess.run([str(binary),'--offline','--no-config','--cache-dir',str(root/'fixtures/zizmor-cache'),'--format','json',str(root/'fixtures'/file)],capture_output=True,text=True)
assert p.returncode in [0,10,11,12,13,14], p.stderr
findings=json.loads(p.stdout)
count=sum(x['ident']=='cache-poisoning' for x in findings)
print(f'{file}: cache-poisoning count={count}; scanner exit={p.returncode}')
expected=0 if 'disabled' in file else 1
assert count==expected, f'expected {expected} cache-poisoning finding, got {count}'

severity: Indirect CI supply-chain blind spot for users relying on zizmor; conditional on an attacker-writable shared cache. No Kache exploit or compromised release demonstrated.

summary: The proposed save-cache:false publishing mitigation does not suppress reads.
checked: Executed unchanged deployed setup bundle in restore-only, backend-disabled and S3 fixture modes; reviewed write/read gates.
closed_by: Tier 1: evidence/restore-only-red.log proves request; evidence/disabled-green.log rejects it; evidence/s3-green.log records sync --pull. This closes a proposed-remediation claim, not an implementation defect against the action contract.
reopens_if: The control is changed to suppress restoration, or an actual read-authentication requirement is supplied.

summary: A normal fork PR is not proven able to poison a release GitHub cache.
checked: Compared source/sink scopes and current low-trust cache-mode policy.
closed_by: Tier 3: GitHub dependency-caching reference merge-ref isolation and read-only low-trust default; documentation snapshot evidence/github-dependency-caching.html.
reopens_if: A production workflow with write-capable override or another same-scope authorized writer is supplied.

summary: No exploitable Kache artifact-integrity defect is admitted by this investigation.
checked: Executed read requests and policy functions; inspected remote acquisition and write gating; did not forge cache artifacts or execute a hosted source-to-sink chain.
closed_by: Tier 1 bounds: localhost service intentionally returned a miss; fake Kache only recorded S3 commands. These do not prove a malicious artifact is accepted.
reopens_if: A fixture supplies hostile artifact bytes accepted and used across the production trust boundary on unchanged Kache.
